To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CO2 emissions embodied by Japan-China trade are significant.

the Japanese economy was confirmed to have been a net importer of CO2 emissions during 1990–2000, while the Chinese economy was a net exporter of CO2 emissions to the Japanese economy during the same time period.

the CO2 emissions embodied from Japan to China were increasing in the 1990-1995 period and then decreased, while the CO2 emissions from Chinese to Japanese exports increased in the first part of the 1995 period and decreased after that.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the CO2 emissions embodied within Japan–China trade, and the results of our study can be used to inform policy makers in the two countries.
the CO2 emissions associated with Japan-China trade and the effects of bilateral trade on CO2 emissions.
the effect of bilateral economic relations on the environmental impact of trade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Japan-China trade has been a double-edged sword.
the bilateral trade between the two countries has helped reduce CO2 emissions in the world.
Japan-China bilateral trade has helped China's CO2 emission reduction and Japan's CO2 emission increase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Japanese economy has become more carbon-intensive in the past decade, while the Chinese economy has been relatively carbon-efficient.
China's economic growth has been achieved at the expense of increased CO2 emissions.
China's economic growth has resulted in increased CO2 emissions in Japan and China.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CO2 emissions from the Japanese-Chinese bilateral trade are a net export from China to Japan.
China's trade with Japan has helped reduce CO2 emissions.
the CO2 emissions embodied by Japan-China trade are not negligible.
